assessments.reasoning: The first purpose bullet in the PROC section makes PROC optional in the EXEC parameter case and constrains its position to the first executable statement when used.

challenge.method: Compared the two adjacent PROC purpose bullets on printed page 155 and the parameter scope continuation on printed page 156. Tested the reading that optionality applies equally to labeled subprocedure PROC.
challenge.results: The next bullet instead requires PROC at a subprocedure start with a label and corresponding END. The cited claim limits optionality and placement to the EXEC parameter case.

limitations: The result does not generalize to PROC in subprocedures or a requirement for the first physical line.
